title: Ramayana Trade Trackers Predict Rs 450 Crore Worldwide by Diwali Day Four
excerpt: Filmibeat predicts the Ranbir Kapoor film might touch Rs 450 crore worldwide on its Diwali Sunday, while Pinkvilla tracks the four-day weekend nearer Rs 490 crore — both figures are trade estimates, not results.
body:
• Trade trackers predict Nitesh Tiwari's Hindi-language Ramayana could touch Rs 450 crore worldwide on Day 4, its Diwali Sunday, according to Filmibeat — a prediction, not a reported result.
  • Estimates for the first three days differ by tracker: Filmibeat puts the worldwide total at Rs 387.25 crore, while Pinkvilla estimates Rs 378 crore, including Rs 214 crore gross in India and Rs 164 crore overseas.
  • Pinkvilla tracks the four-day extended weekend higher still, at around USD 23 million overseas and Rs 490 crore worldwide — again, a projection the tracker labels a subjective trade estimate.
  • For diaspora audiences, the United States delivered USD 7.225 million of the three-day overseas total, and Pinkvilla reports the film set a biggest-ever single day for a Bollywood release there on Saturday.

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana, the Hindi-language mythological drama led by Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Raavan, has become the centre of box office discussion over its first weekend. The question trade trackers are asking on Day 4 — Diwali Sunday, November 8 — is not what the film has collected, but what it might: Filmibeat predicts the film is expected to see a hike in numbers on the occasion of Diwali, enter the Rs 400 crore club and possibly touch the Rs 450 crore mark worldwide, while also entering the Rs 200 crore mark in the overseas market in four days.

What the first three days actually show — as estimates

Box office figures at this stage are trade estimates, and the trackers do not agree. Filmibeat reports that Ramayana minted Rs 387.25 crore in three days at the worldwide box office. Pinkvilla, in its own reporting, puts the three-day worldwide take lower, at Rs 378 crore, combining Rs 214 crore gross in India with a three-day overseas cumulative of USD 17.45 million, or about Rs 164 crore. Pinkvilla states in its disclaimer that its figures are subjective trade estimates compiled from commercial parameters and advance trends, and do not constitute finalised collections or certified accounting statements. Readers should treat both totals the same way.

On Day 4 itself, Filmibeat reports an India net collection of Rs 40.69 crore until 6 p.m., including Rs 27.99 crore in Hindi, Rs 5.57 crore in Kannada, Rs 4.71 crore from Telugu and Rs 2.42 crore in Tamil, taking the overall India net collection to Rs 223.39 crore so far on the day. Those are partial-day figures, not a closed Day 4 total.

Two different Day 4 forecasts

The forecasts diverge as much as the reported totals. Filmibeat's prediction is that the film might touch Rs 450 crore worldwide after the opening weekend. Pinkvilla tracks the four-day extended opening weekend higher, at around USD 23 million overseas and Rs 490 crore worldwide. Neither figure has been collected yet; both are projections published while Day 4 trading was still under way, and the gap between them is a reminder of how much of a Diwali Sunday depends on evening and night shows.

"I have just watched Ramayana, and I really, really liked it. I want every Indian to go and watch Ramayana because this film is no less than any Hollywood film."

— Sunny Deol, who plays Hanuman in Ramayana, as quoted by Filmibeat

The film and the response so far

Ramayana is inspired by Valmiki's Ramayana and is made in two parts. Alongside Kapoor, Pallavi and Yash, the cast features Ravi Dubey, Sunny Deol as Hanuman, Anupam Kher, Lara Dutta, Arun Govil, Rakul Preet Singh and Vivek Oberoi, and Filmibeat puts its reported budget at Rs 1,700 crore. Filmibeat reports a mixed opening response: after a slower-than-expected opening day, reportedly below the Rs 80 crore mark, the film dipped on day two before improving on day three, while its visual effects have sparked debate online and Yash's screen presence as Raavan has drawn strong attention.

Why the overseas numbers matter

The clearest strength in Pinkvilla's reporting is overseas. It reports that Saturday's overseas collection of USD 7.30 million, about Rs 69 crore, was the biggest single overseas day ever for an Indian film, surpassing Baahubali: The Conclusion, which had collected just under USD 7 million on its Saturday. In the United States, it reports, the film registered the biggest single day ever for a Bollywood release, overtaking Dhurandhar: The Revenge, and the United Kingdom grossed GBP 750,000 on Saturday, surpassing the previous single-day record by around 15 per cent. For North American audiences, the film is playing in theatres now; whether it lands near Rs 450 crore or Rs 490 crore will only be known when the weekend closes and the trackers publish their final estimates.
